# PUT /api/v1/user/blocks/{username}

Block a user

**Module:** [routers](../modules/routers.md) · **Auth:** bearer · **ID:** `ep-192`

## Request

| Param | Location | Type | Required |
|-------|----------|------|----------|
| username | path | string | True |
| note | query | string | False |

**Headers:** `Authorization`

## Response

**204** — empty

- **404** — User not found by username
- **400** — Cannot block (self, org member, already blocked by target, or not authorized)
- **422** — Cannot block organization

## Business Rules

| Rule | Category | Condition |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Cannot block yourself | authorization | blocker.ID == blockee.ID |
| Cannot block the doer themselves | authorization | doer.ID == blockee.ID |
| Cannot block an organization | validation | blockee.IsOrganization() |
| Cannot block user who already blocks you | authorization | user_model.IsUserBlockedBy(ctx, blockee, blocker.ID) |
| Cannot block org member (when blocker is org) | authorization | blocker.IsOrganization() && isMember |
| Only org owner or admin can block on behalf of org | authorization | blocker.IsOrganization() && !isAdmin && !doer.IsAdmin |
| Blocking unfollows both users from each other | business_logic | Block operation succeeds validation |
| Blocking removes all shared repository relationships | business_logic | Block operation succeeds validation |
| Admin users bypass block checks (IsUserBlockedBy returns false for admins) | authorization | blockee.IsAdmin |

### Error Paths

- **Username not found** → shared.BlockUser → 404
- **ErrCanNotBlock or ErrBlockOrganization** → shared.BlockUser → 400
- **DB error in transaction** → shared.BlockUser → 500

## ⚠️ Performance Issues

| Severity | Type | Description | Recommendation |
|----------|------|-------------|----------------|
| high | n_plus_1_queries | Multiple paginated loops (unstarRepos, unwatchRepos, unassignIssues, removeCollaborations) each perform per-item operations inside loops | Use batch DELETE operations instead of per-item loops. Consider async processing for cleanup operations. |
| medium | synchronous_blocking | All cleanup operations (unstar, unwatch, unassign, remove collaborations, cancel transfers) run synchronously in a single transaction | Consider splitting cleanup into async background job, only the blocking record insert needs to be synchronous |

### Optimization Recommendations

- **[P1] query_optimization**: Replace paginated per-item loops with batch DELETE statements — *Impact: Reduce from O(n) queries to O(1) per cleanup type*
- **[P2] async**: Move cleanup operations to background job — *Impact: Reduce API response time from potentially seconds to milliseconds*

## 🛡️ Resiliency

**Risk Level:** high

| Pattern | Status | Severity | Detail |
|---------|--------|----------|--------|
| non_atomic | ✅ configured | medium | All operations wrapped in db.WithTx, so atomicity is maintained. However, the transaction is very long-running for users with many shared resources. |
| idempotency | ✅ configured | low | UNIQUE constraint on (blocker_id, blockee_id) prevents duplicate blocks. Retry would fail with constraint violation. |
| timeout | ❌ missing | high | No timeout on the transaction. With many shared resources, the paginated cleanup loops could run for a very long time. |

**Cascading failure risk:** Long transaction could hold locks on multiple tables (follow, star, watch, issue_assignees, collaboration, repo_transfer), potentially blocking other operations

**Graceful degradation:** none
